title: Alliance Shadow Assassin
next_chapter_hook: Just as everyone thought the dust had settled, the eerie smile on the betrayer's face as he lay dying made Chen Ji realize—he had missed something in his deduction.

text.content: Ye Qing's delicate fragrance still lingered at his nostrils, but Chen Ji had already concealed every trace of tenderness. He stood with hands clasped behind his back by the window, moonlight stretching his shadow long and thin, like a blade蓄势待发. His fingertips unconsciously traced the warm Jade Slip hidden in his sleeve—the contact token Ye Qing left behind, and one of tonight's variables. Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed in his mind, carrying a hint of scrutiny: 'Do you trust her?' Chen Ji's lips curved slightly, the smile not reaching his eyes: 'Trust is irrelevant. What matters is that her interests align with mine at this moment.'

The Tianji Record Fragment slowly emerged in his Mental Sea. Chen Ji closed his eyes and began deducing all possible variables for tonight. But at a crucial juncture, the vision suddenly blurred—a familiar interference, as if someone had deliberately torn a rift in the web of fate. Chen Ji's brow furrowed tightly. What appeared in his Mental Sea was not a clear image, but a face all too familiar to him—that was... 'How is this possible.' He murmured, his voice carrying a rare tremor. Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment before saying: 'The Tianji Record never lies. Do you wish to see it?'

Chen Ji slowly nodded. The scene in his Mental Sea gradually cleared, yet made him feel as if plunged into an ice abyss—there stood a person he had personally rescued from death's edge, someone he once believed he could entrust his back to. Now, that person stood in the shadow of a Holy Sect envoy, presenting a blood-stained confidential document with both hands. And the seal on that document was none other than Chen Ji's personal mark. Rage burned in his chest like wildfire, but Chen Ji's expression grew increasingly calm—a deathly stillness before the storm. 'I've noted it.' He said quietly, each word seeming to be挤出 from between his teeth: 'Yes, I've noted it.'

dialogue.content: 'What do you plan to do?' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a hint of inquiry: 'Handle it privately, end it cleanly, or...' Chen Ji interrupted him: 'No.' The word was decisive, without any hesitation: 'Since he dared betray, he must prepare to bear the consequences—not just his alone, but the price for all who harbor ill intentions. I want the world to see the fate of those who betray the Tianqing Sect Alliance.' Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a long while before a meaningful sigh resonated through the Mental Sea: 'You're more of a chess player than I imagined. However... killing a chicken to warn monkeys won't necessarily frighten off true ambitious schemers.'

text.content: The next morning, the atmosphere in the Alliance Council Hall was heavy. Chen Ji sat at the last seat, expressionless, as if last night's shocking discovery had never occurred. In a corner of the hall, a middle-aged man in a green robe was conversing quietly with several elders, wearing a humble and fawning smile—that was Zhou Yan, the Alliance's Chief of Intelligence, and a trusted subordinate Chen Ji had personally promoted when he joined the Alliance. His gaze toward Chen Ji carried concern and loyalty; no one could find any flaw. Chen Ji met his eyes and nodded slightly. That warm smile made the wariness in Zhou Yan's eyes diminish. Yet no one noticed Chen Ji's hand gently stroking a dark gold token hidden in his sleeve.

Han Lie sprawled carelessly across from Chen Ji, his black iron heavy sword resting casually against the chair. His attitude toward Chen Ji had subtly shifted lately—though still disliking this 'waste,' after several battles side by side, that pure disgust had mixed with a hint of awkward recognition. Now, noticing Chen Ji's unusual demeanor, he frowned: 'Hey, why do you look like death today? Who owes you money?' Chen Ji raised his eyes to look at him. That calm, wave-less gaze made Han Lie inexplicably shudder. 'Brother Han,' Chen Ji suddenly spoke, 'what punishment do you think a traitor deserves?'

dialogue.content: Han Lie was taken aback, then answered brazenly: 'A traitor? Hmph, with this young master's temperament, I'd cut him in two with one blade, clean and efficient!' He paused, his eyes rolling: 'What, did you discover someone betraying the Alliance? Who's tired of living? Tell me, I'll handle him personally!' Chen Ji looked at his eager expression and suddenly smiled. That gentle, harmless smile made Han Lie inexplicably feel a chill—he had seen Chen Ji smile like this before. The last time he smiled like that, an elder's entire family vanished from the sect within three days.

text.content: Just then, commotion erupted outside the hall. A blood-soaked scout was helped in, gasping: 'Terrible! The Xuanwu Sect border was attacked, three posts completely annihilated!' The hall erupted in an uproar. The Alliance elders exchanged horrified glances—the Xuanwu Sect was one of the three great sects! Who would dare provoke them? At this moment, Chen Ji slowly rose, his voice not loud but clearly audible to everyone: 'Everyone, please wait. Let me explain this for you.' He surveyed the surroundings, his gaze finally landing on Zhou Yan in the corner: 'Chief Zhou, are you aware of this?'

Zhou Yan's smile froze for an instant, then quickly returned to normal, so fast almost no one noticed. He hurried forward, feigning alarm: 'What does Brother Chen mean? How could I know about such a major border attack?' Chen Ji stared at him quietly, that gaze as still as a dead pool of water, yet flickering with an edge in certain moments. 'Is that so?' he said softly. 'Then who leaked the defensive formations of those three posts? When was the scout's return route monitored?' He walked step by step toward Zhou Yan, each step striking like a chord in everyone's heart: 'Chief Zhou, how much did the Holy Sect pay you? Enough to buy your life?'

The hall exploded at these words. Zhou Yan's face instantly turned pale, then flushed crimson as he shouted: 'Brother Chen, you slander me! I've been loyal to the Alliance—how can you—' Before he finished, the dark gold token from Chen Ji's sleeve shot out, firmly embedding into the floor tiles at Zhou Yan's feet. The token's front bore an ancient 'Covenant' character, while the back displayed the Holy Sect's hidden pattern—the token used exclusively when the Holy Sect signed loyalty pacts with insiders. Zhou Yan seemed strangled, his voice cutting off abruptly, his entire body chilled to the bone. 'This item,' Chen Ji's voice cold as a poisoned blade, 'was found in the hidden compartment under your bed. Need I continue?'

Zhou Yan's legs went soft, nearly collapsing. His desperate gaze swept around, searching for help, but the elders who had smiled at him now wore icy expressions, several already touching their weapons. In despair, he suddenly let out a hoarse, wild laugh: 'Good! Good one, Chen Ji! Zhou Yan concedes defeat!' He abruptly looked up, a fierce glint flashing in his eyes: 'But do you think you've won? Do you think removing me changes anything? Let me tell you—the Holy Sect has far stronger powers behind them, powers you cannot imagine!' Chen Ji watched his collapse with an unchanged expression: 'So, is this your final statement?'

choice.prompt: Zhou Yan's betrayal has been publicly exposed with irrefutable evidence. Yet faced with this traitor he once trusted but who now sold everything, Chen Ji must make a choice—

choices.description: Before the entire Alliance, deal with Zhou Yan in the harshest manner, letting everyone see the consequences of betrayal. This is an answer to the loyal and a warning to potential traitors.
choices.visible_cost: May provoke stronger retaliation from the Holy Sect
choices.visible_reward: The Alliance's internal cohesion greatly increases, Chen Ji's prestige soars
choices.risk_hint: The Holy Sect may accelerate its attacks on the Alliance

text.content: Chen Ji's voice echoed through the hall, cold and resolute: 'Bring Zhou Yan to the execution platform and announce to the world his crime of betraying the sect.' He surveyed the surroundings, his gaze sweeping across every face of fear or shock: 'Everyone, today's matter is the iron law of the Alliance—those who betray their master for personal gain will be hunted to the ends of the earth.' Han Lie was the first to slam the table and cheer, followed by waves of agreement throughout the hall. Chen Ji's name was for the first time spoken with genuine reverence.

choices.text: Return Kindness for Grudge·Spare His Life
choices.description: Don't kill Zhou Yan, instead publicly abolish his cultivation, leaving him alive. This shows Chen Ji's leniency while being a crueler humiliation—letting the traitor live out his humiliated remaining years.
choices.visible_cost: Some may think Chen Ji is soft-hearted, weakening the warning effect
choices.visible_reward: Chen Ji gains a reputation for 'benevolence and righteousness,' while making Zhou Yan's life worse than death
choices.risk_hint: Zhou Yan may become a chess piece for enemies to turn against him

text.content: Chen Ji walked slowly toward Zhou Yan, who had collapsed on the ground, and whispered a few words into his ear. No one knew what Chen Ji said. All they saw was Zhou Yan's complexion shift from pallid white to iron-green, then from iron-green to death-gray, as though he had heard something more terrifying than death itself. Chen Ji straightened up, his voice unruffled: 'Strip his cultivation, expel him from the alliance, life or death is irrelevant.' This was more chilling than simply killing him—a former Director of Intelligence who had lost his cultivation, whose grudges and enemies were scattered across the world, his days ahead... The way people looked at Chen Ji now carried not just reverence, but an added layer of unfathomable wariness.

choices.text: 'Turn Foes into Blades, Bend Them to Your Will'
choices.description: Zhou Yan possessed extensive internal secrets of the Holy Sect. Chen Ji decided to turn this scheme to his advantage, making Zhou Yan a chess piece for the alliance to conduct reverse infiltration of the Holy Sect. This approach carried extremely high risk, but the potential gains were equally staggering.
choices.visible_cost: Need to expend additional Heavenly Fate in the Tianji Record to conceal the flaws in his betrayal memories
choices.visible_reward: Gain a deep-planted spy within the Holy Sect, and Zhou Yan becomes a handle under Chen Ji's control
choices.risk_hint: Once Zhou Yan recovers part of his memories or is examined by higher-level Holy Sect secret arts, the consequences would be unthinkable

text.content: Chen Ji leaned down and spoke a sentence into Zhou Yan's ear. What that sentence was, no one knew. They only saw a诡异 light suddenly flash through Zhou Yan's originally despairing eyes, like a drowning man grasping at a lifeline. He kowtowed tremblingly: 'Subordinate... is willing to serve Young Master Chen unto death.' This scene was too bizarre; many harbored suspicions in their hearts, but gazing at Chen Ji's indifferent smile, they dared not ask more. Mo Xiansheng sneered within the Mental Sea: 'Are you certain you can control him?' Chen Ji answered in his heart: 'What if I can't control him? He's already a dead piece, but I can make his death worthwhile.'

dialogue.content: After the matter was concluded, Han Lie stepped forward, having难得 tucked away his usual arrogant demeanor. He stared at Chen Ji for a long while before suddenly speaking: 'Fellow... I underestimated you before.' After a pause, he added another sentence, carrying a hint of reluctant acknowledgment in his tone, 'But this move of yours today was indeed splendid. If it were me, there's no way I could've done it so... so clean and tidy without leaving any evidence.' He crossed his arms, the玄铁重剑 swaying on his shoulder, 'Next time something like this happens, remember to call me. Though I'm good at fighting, this business of scheming... you're indeed a cut above me, just a little.' This was probably the closest thing to 'admitting defeat' Han Lie could ever say.

Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out in the Mental Sea, carrying a complex undertone: 'Your handling today, no matter which approach, far exceeded my expectations.' He paused, 'But Zhou Yan's words before death... 'Behind the Holy Sect exists an even stronger being'—how do you plan to investigate this?' Chen Ji did not answer immediately. He gazed at the water stain left by the dragged-away Zhou Yan—the floor soaked by his terrified cold sweat, gleaming sharply in the morning light. Long after, he finally spoke in his heart: 'Investigate? No, now is not the time.' Mo Xiansheng pressed: 'Then when will be the time?' A cold smile curled at Chen Ji's lips: 'When they come to me of their own accord.'

text.content: After the council meeting, Chen Ji remained alone in the empty great hall. Hands clasped behind his back, he stood facing the stone pillar engraved with the names of successive alliance sect masters, his gaze deep as an abyss. Zhou Yan's matter was merely a beginning, a small ripple提前 captured by the Tianji Record. What truly unsettled his mind was the question that had always lingered—the Eye of Heavenly Providence. Mo Xiansheng had said the Tianji Record was merely one of the piecesHeavenly Will had placed in the mortal world. So then, the Holy Sect behind Zhou Yan—on whose chessboard did they rest? And himself, was he currently walking along some fate script that had long been written?

Footsteps sounded outside the hall, and Chen Ji收敛了 all his thoughts. The visitor was Su Qingyao's attendant, delivering a jade talisman—the exclusive communication token of an Inner Disciple Senior Fellow. Su Qingyao had written only one sentence in the talisman: 'Tonight at the Hour of the Rat, beneath the old locust tree in the Rear Mountain, there is important business to discuss.' Chen Ji held the warm jade talisman, his eyes flickering slightly. This Inner Disciple Senior Fellow had repeatedly tried to probe his secrets, yet he had skillfully deflected every attempt with his arrangements. Now she had taken the initiative to invite him—he wondered what new suspicions she had uncovered. He tucked the jade talisman into his sleeve, a playful curve forming at his lips: 'Senior Fellow Su, you are indeed persistent.'

At the Hour of the Rat, in the Rear Mountain, the old locust tree's branches rustled in the night wind. Chen Ji arrived as promised, only to find Su Qingyao had been waiting for quite some time. Moonlight filtered through the gaps in the leaves, casting mottled light on her cold, clear profile. This Inner Disciple Senior Fellow who was usually high and mighty, now standing alone beneath the moon, surprisingly revealed a trace of imperceptible exhaustion. She turned to face him, her gaze like a sword, piercing directly toward Chen Ji: 'The Zhou Yan affair was orchestrated by you.' This was not a question, but a definite statement. Chen Ji blinked, his expression innocent: 'What does Senior Sister Su mean by this? The traitor has been executed, yet why do you blame me instead?'

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao coldly laughed: 'Zhou Yan joined the alliance for three years, loyal and devoted, never a single misconduct. You've been in the alliance for only half a year, yet you've captured him—if it weren't premeditated, how could you be so precise?' She stepped forward, nearly face to face with Chen Ji, 'Chen Ji, who exactly are you?' Chen Ji gazed at her quietly, their shadows mingling together beneath the moonlight. He suddenly smiled—that smile was so mild it made hearts tremble: 'Since Senior Sister Su doesn't trust me, why bother arranging this meeting?' His voice was very soft, yet carried a certain soul-subduing power, 'You could simply report me to the elders—as long as you have evidence.' Su Qingyao was choked, her chest rising and falling slightly, clearly furious.

text.content: The two confronted each other for a long while before Su Qingyao was the first to look away. She took a deep breath, her voice recovering its usual coldness: 'Forget it. Tonight I summoned you not to pursue this matter.' She drew a broken jade slip from her sleeve and extended it to Chen Ji, 'This was another item found in Zhou Yan's secret chamber, engraved with the Holy Sect's covert markings. I couldn't understand it, but I thought perhaps you could.' Chen Ji accepted the jade slip, his spiritual sense probing within, and his pupils abruptly constricted—the contents recorded fragments concerning the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key,' and among the names mentioned, one nearly caused his composed expression to lose control: 'Chen Nian.'

In that instant, a great storm raged in Chen Ji's heart. But his expression only changed at that initial moment, then quickly returned to its usual tranquility. He tucked the jade slip into his sleeve and nodded to Su Qingyao: 'Thank you, Senior Sister Su.' Su Qingyao gazed at him intently, trying to discern something from that impassive face, yet seeing only an abyss of unfathomable darkness. She suddenly felt a pang of regret for handing this thing over to him—her intuition told her this man was far more dangerous than she had imagined. 'Chen Ji,' she spoke, her voice carrying a softness she herself had not noticed, 'What exactly are you scheming?' Chen Ji turned to look at her, moonlight outlining his silhouette like it was carved by a blade: 'Senior Sister Su, this question—when you truly wish to know the answer someday, then I'll tell you.'

Night wind brushed past, dispersing the sound of Chen Ji's departing footsteps. Su Qingyao stood alone beneath the old locust tree, gazing at the gradually vanishing figure, an indescribable emotion welling in her heart. She had seen too many geniuses and great schemers, yet never anyone like Chen Ji—clearly just a servant disciple, yet seeming as though he controlled the entire world's chess game. The secrets he carried were too many, so many that she no longer wished to pursue them. But one thing she was certain of: whatever Chen Ji was scheming, she did not want to be his enemy. Moonlight flowed like water, Su Qingyao softly sighed, and turned to vanish into the night. And beyond her perception, Chen Ji's figure reemerged from the shadows, gazing toward the direction she had departed, a meaningful glint flickering in his eyes.
